Almost every small business owner I know has AI on their phone. Almost none of them have it working inside their business.

The Census Bureau put a number on it: about 37% of companies with 250+ employees are using AI. Businesses with four people or fewer? Less than one in five.

Same tools. Same apps. It's not an access problem — it's a capacity problem.

Three questions to know if you're ready:
→ When someone reaches out, does anything answer before you do?
→ Does your follow-up happen without somebody having to remember it?
→ Could you step away for two weeks and still keep booking?

If any answer is no, that's fixable.

Two minutes, twelve questions — link in bio.

We're all competing for a sliver of attention. Here's the question nobody asks: once you get it, what do you do with it?

Content got easy. AI is pumping it out at lightning speed. The ones who win are the ones with a system on the other side to catch it.
